structure, not read from an annotation, and ClinVar's own consequence field is held back to
mark it.

sensors and its activity is a monotone transform of the folding ddG. confirmed
C5 FAIL  (gate: activity BELOW 0.5 -- destabilising should mean more pathogenic)
THE SENSOR POINTS THE WRONG WAY. Activity is 0.5194, outside the shuffle band on
the wrong side: within a gene, the MORE destabilising a substitution is scored, the
LESS likely it is to be pathogenic. That is backwards from the mechanism nexus
claims, and the margin (0.0194 against a band of 0.0123) is thin
enough that on 55,337 variants statistical significance says almost nothing about
usefulness. The most likely cause is domain shift: ddg_model was fitted on SKEMPI
interface mutations in crystal structures and is being asked about whole AlphaFold
monomers, where benign variants concentrate in low-confidence disordered regions.

THE CHAIN IS BUILT AND THE MIDDLE LINK IS VERIFIED. 56,258 point mutations go
from a genomic coordinate, through measured torsion, to a computed residue change, into
nexus -- and the residue step agrees with ClinVar's own consequence call on 99.99%,
having never been shown it.
THE FOLD LINK IS GENE-LEVEL, AS PREDECLARED. Torsion varies within only 55.7% of
multi-variant genes and does not separate pathogenic from benign inside a gene. It is a
real measurement attached at the right coordinate, and it cannot tell two mutations in
one gene apart, which is what the question asked for.
